etymology: Back-formation from "patriotainment": the performer the format cannot run without
occasion: A commercial break that needs a grievance to sell the next segment.
call: "Folks, they don't want you to know this."
tell: Every segment ends on a sponsor read
Owns the flag as a prop and licenses the footage
No position survives a ratings dip
counter: Ask what was withheld and who was paid. The audience is the product, and the "they" is usually the sponsor.

confused_with.tell: The playtriot performs for free and believes it; the patriotainer performs on contract and invoices for it.
The format is the show; the patriotainer is the person the show is built around - and the one who gets replaced when the timeslot moves.

senses: The on-air performer who converts national identity into a segment: hired to be certain, paid to be angry, and never once required to be right.
A broadcaster whose only consistent commitment is the next hour of programming. The flag is a prop, the outrage is inventory, and moral clarity is a liability no sponsor will underwrite.
example: *"He spent one segment mourning the republic and the next selling the supplement that would save it - a **patriotainer** to the last ad break."*
